name: MoSCoW Prioritization
use_case: A scope-negotiation technique that sorts requirements into Must have, Should have, Could have and Won't have this time, so a fixed deadline is met by agreeing in advance what gets dropped rather than by discovering it under pressure. Best used with stakeholders at the start of a time-boxed delivery, when the release date is immovable, the wish list exceeds the budget, and someone needs to say out loud which items are genuinely non-negotiable.
strengths: the explicit Won't-have list makes descoping a decision instead of a failure
categories are understandable to non-technical stakeholders immediately
pairs naturally with fixed-date, variable-scope delivery
very fast for a first pass over a large requirement list
weaknesses: everything drifts into Must have unless someone enforces a cap
gives no ordering inside a category, so it can't sequence the work
no notion of cost or effort, only of desirability
the boundary between Should and Could is often argued rather than reasoned
